title: How I built a $200-a-week TikTok micro-video side hustle with AI tools
excerpt: I turned AI-generated 30-second TikTok videos into a steady $200-weekly side income. Here’s the workflow, costs, and realistic earnings you can expect.
metaDescription: Learn a realistic, step-by-step workflow for creating and selling AI-generated 30-second TikTok videos to small businesses. I share tools, pricing, and earnings
author: Ali Hamza
coverImageAlt: Person planning work with notebook and coffee
body:
## Why I tried AI-generated TikTok videos
I keep hearing that short-form video is the fastest way to get attention online. The hype made me wonder if I could sell ready-made 30-second clips to local businesses without spending hours editing. I set up a workflow that relies only on affordable AI tools.

## The tool stack I settled on
- Script writing: ChatGPT (free tier) for quick copy.
- Voice-over: ElevenLabs (free credits, then $5/mo for 10k characters).
- Video assembly: Pictory (starts at $19/mo) to stitch stock footage, text, and voice.
- Export & delivery: Gumroad for instant digital product sales.
I chose these because each has a low entry price and a web UI that doesn’t require a powerful PC. If you already have a favorite stock footage source, you can swap it in.

## Step-by-step workflow (no fluff)
1. Find a niche - I targeted local coffee shops that want a quick "new drink" promo. The niche is narrow enough to personalize but broad enough to repeat.
2. Create a prompt - In ChatGPT I typed: "Write a 30-second script for a TikTok video announcing a seasonal latte, include a call to action to visit the shop." The output gave me three sentence blocks and a hook.
3. Generate voice - I pasted the script into ElevenLabs, chose a warm mid-range voice, and downloaded the MP3.
4. Assemble video - In Pictory I uploaded the voice file, selected "text-to-video" mode, and let the AI match stock clips to each line. I tweaked the timing to keep the total under 30 seconds.
5. Add branding - A quick overlay of the shop's logo (provided by the client) and a final screen with the address.
6. Export - 1080p MP4, about 5 MB, ready to upload.
7. List on Gumroad - I created a product called "30-second TikTok promo for [Coffee Shop]" with a $30 price point.

## Cost breakdown per video
- ChatGPT: free within usage limits.
- ElevenLabs: roughly $0.10 per 30-second clip after the free credits.
- Pictory: $0.30-$0.50 per video when you amortize the $19/mo subscription over 40 videos a month.
- Gumroad fees: 5% + $0.30 per sale.
- Total per video: about $1-$2 in direct costs.
That means each $30 sale nets roughly $27 before taxes.

## Finding the first customers
I didn’t rely on cold-email spamming. Instead I:
- Scouted Instagram - Looked for local cafés posting static menus but no video.
- Commented with value - Offered a free 10-second teaser in the comment thread.
- Follow-up DM - Sent a short message: "I made a quick TikTok promo for you. Want the full version for $30?"
The personal touch got replies from three owners within a week. Two paid instantly; the third asked for a revision, which I delivered for free to keep the relationship warm.

## Early results
- Videos sold: 8
- Gross revenue: $240
- Platform & tool fees: about $15
- Net profit: about $225
I consider $225 a realistic weekly figure once you have a steady pipeline of 2-3 new clients per week. The numbers reflect the time spent on outreach and occasional revisions.

## Scaling tips (without burning out)
- Template the script - Keep a folder of 5-10 generic hooks you can swap in seconds.
- Batch voice generation - Generate voice-overs for multiple scripts in one ElevenLabs session to avoid repeated clicks.
- Outsource revisions - Hire a junior freelancer on Upwork for $5-$10 per tweak once you have a cash cushion.
- Automate delivery - Use Zapier to send the Gumroad download link automatically when a payment is confirmed.

## FAQ
**Q: Do I need a professional video editor to make these clips look good?**
A: Not really. The AI in Pictory does most of the heavy lifting. A few manual tweaks (cropping, timing) are enough to make the final product feel custom.

**Q: What if a client wants a longer video?**
A: Offer a tiered pricing model: $30 for 30 seconds, $55 for 60 seconds, $80 for 90 seconds. The extra time adds a bit more editing but the workflow stays the same.

## Bottom line
AI tools let you turn a simple script into a polished TikTok video in under 15 minutes. With a $30 price tag, low overhead, and modest outreach effort, you can reliably pull in $200-$300 a week. It’s not a get-rich-quick scheme, but it is a repeatable micro-service that fits nicely into a freelancer's existing workload.
